The louder she got, the harder he pushed. So she tried it backwards. 🔄

Jesse was six, and he ran everywhere. "Stop!" "Back in bed!" Nothing worked. So his mom tried three "reverse parenting" tricks:

1️⃣ Show a little weakness. Not fake, just true.
"There are so many cars. Can you hold my hand, so I feel safe?"

2️⃣ Give him an important job.
"She calms down when you sing. Will you be her helper?"

3️⃣ Don't know everything.
"My tower keeps falling. Can you show me how?"

In one study, kids asked to BE helpers helped more than kids just asked to help. When kids feel needed, they don't have to fight to feel big. They grow. 🌱

Two years later, Mom had the hardest day of her year. Jesse sat down beside her, took her hand, and said, "It's okay, Mom. Hold my hand. I'll help you feel safe." ❤️

She thought she was teaching him to listen. She was teaching him to love.

Jesus does this too. He didn't need a little boy's lunch to feed five thousand people. "There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish." (John 6:9, ESV) He chose to use it anyway. Then He let His own body be broken on the cross for our sins, and rose again, to bring us home. He doesn't need our help. He invites it. ✝️

📌 Save this for the next time the battle starts.
